papers.title: Boxes in Infinite Words: Complexity, Automata, and Point Modules
papers.abstract: Motivated by the geometry of point modules over monomial algebras, we introduce a box-counting function associated to a right-infinite word over a finite alphabet. An extendable box is a family of finite words obtained by choosing letters independently at each position, subject to the condition that all choices admit a common infinite right continuation in the associated subshift. We prove several results for these functions for words of linearly bounded complexity. For $k$-automatic words, we show using techniques from first-order logic that the total box-counting function is $k$-regular. Finally, we apply our results to prove eventual affine growth of the number of positive-dimensional irreducible components in finite projections of point-module spaces associated to semiprime monomial algebras of at most quadratic growth.

papers.title: Cohomological VC-density: Bounds and Applications
papers.abstract: The concept of Vapnik-Chervonenkis (VC) density is pivotal across various mathematical fields, including discrete geometry, probability theory and model theory. In this paper, we introduce a topological generalization of VC-density. Let $Y$ be a topological space and $\mathcal{X}$ a family of closed subspaces of $Y$. For each $p \geq 0$, we define a number, $\mathrm{vcd}^{p}_{\mathcal{X}}$, which we refer to as the degree $p$ VC-density of the family $\mathcal{X}$. The classical notion of VC-density within this topological framework can be recovered by setting $p=0$. Our definition of degree $p$ VC-density extends to higher orders as well. For $p \geq 0$, $q \geq 1$, we define the degree $p$, order $q$ VC density $\mathrm{vcd}^{p,q}_{\mathcal{X}}$ of $\mathcal{X}$, which recovers Shelah's notion of higher order VC-density for $q$-dependent families when $p=0$. Our definition introduces a completely new notion when $p > 0$. We examine the properties of $\mathrm{vcd}_{\mathcal{X}}^p$ (as well as $\mathrm{vcd}^{p,q}_{\mathcal{X}}$) when the families $\mathcal{X}$ are definable in structures with some underlying topology (for instance, the Euclidean topology for o-minimal structures over $\mathbb{R}$, the analytic topology over $\mathbb{C}$, or the \'{e}tale site for schemes over arbitrary algebraically closed fields). Our main result establishes that in any model of these theories \[ \mathrm{vcd}_{\mathcal{X}}^p \leq (p+1) \dim X, \] and more generally for any $q \geq 1$ \[ \mathrm{vcd}^{p,q}_{\mathcal{X}} \leq (p+q) \dim X. \] We give examples to show that our bounds are optimal. We also present combinatorial applications of our higher-degree VC-density bounds, deriving higher degree topological analogs of well-known results such as the existence of $\varepsilon$-nets and the fractional Helly theorem.

papers.title: Hilbert's Tenth problem and NP-completeness of Boolean Syllogistic with unordered cartesian product
papers.abstract: We relate the decidability problem for BS with unordered cartesian product with Hilbert's Tenth problem and prove that BS with unordered cartesian product is NP-complete.

papers.title: Relative computability and definability for nonregular oracles
papers.abstract: Classically, a set is computable from an oracle if both the set and its complement are computably enumerable (c.e.) relative to that oracle. We construct a countable nonstandard model of true arithmetic with sets A and X such that both A and its complement are c.e. relative to X, yet A is not pointwise Turing reducible to X. The Turing functionals used here are single-valued at every oracle. For regular oracles, we prove that the classical equivalence holds over ISigma_1. Two further phenomena, each known from earlier work, are realized with the same oracle X that witnesses our main separation. Strong and pointwise Turing reducibility differ for this X, and some Delta_1^X set is not X-c.e.

papers.title: Maximality of the Do\v{s}en-Petri\'{c} Boolean Category
papers.abstract: We prove that the zero-identity Boolean category of Do\v{s}en and Petri\'c, freely generated by a nonempty set of propositional variables, is maximal. Every congruence preserved by the operations on morphisms and by uniform formula substitution either is equality or identifies every pair of parallel morphisms. This disproves their conjecture that the category is not maximal. We give two proofs that use Boolean Coherence and uniform formula substitution to derive equality of the product projections from an identification of distinct parallel morphisms. We also give a Lean formalization of these proofs and their dependencies. It includes Boolean Coherence and the correspondence between substitution on tagged occurrence sets and substitution on finite ordinals.

papers.title: On non-isomorphic universal sofic groups
papers.abstract: We show that there are $2^{\aleph_0}$ non-isomorphic universal sofic groups. This proves a conjecture of Simon Thomas.

papers.title: On $(\Sigma^2_1)^{uB}$ Absoluteness Between V and HOD
papers.abstract: We put together Woodin's $\Sigma^2_1$ basis theorem of AD$^+$ and Vop\v{e}nka's theorem to conclude the following: If there is a proper class of Woodin cardinals, then every $(\Sigma^2_1)^{\mbox{uB}}$ statement that is true in $V$ is true in $\mbox{HOD}$. Moreover, this is true even if we allow a parameter $C \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ such that $C$ and its complement have scales that are $\mbox{OD}$ and universally Baire. We also investigate whether $(\Sigma^2_1)^{\mbox{uB}}$ statements are upwards absolute from $\mbox{HOD}$ to $V$ under large cardinal hypotheses, observing that this is true if $\mbox{HOD}$ has a proper class of Woodin cardinals. Finally, we discuss $(\forall^{\mathbb{R}})\, (\Sigma^2_1)^{\mbox{uB}}$ absoluteness and conclude that this much absoluteness between $\mbox{HOD}$ and $V$ cannot be implied by any large cardinal axiom consistent with the axiom ``$V =$ Ultimate $L$''.

papers.title: A Dubnov-Ivanov-Nagata-Higman Theorem for NIP nilrings
papers.abstract: We prove that NIP nilrings of bounded nilexponent are nilpotent. We also deduce that NIP $\omega$-categorical $n$-Engel Lie algebras of characteristic $p>n$ are nilpotent, yielding a case of the Lie algebra analogous of Wilson conjecture for $\omega$-categorical groups.
